label: Morning Brief
timezoneNote: All times shown in ET (America/New_York). Items marked headline were written only from the publisher's headline and summary.

driver.text: Per WSJ, Asian equities slumped as the rout in artificial-intelligence-linked stocks continued, sending tech-heavy indexes toward bear-market territory (3:51 AM ET), while Nasdaq futures recovered some ground ahead of U.S. jobs data due later Friday (5:06 AM ET). Bloomberg reported Taiwan authorized its National Financial Stabilization Fund to support its stock market (5:35 AM ET) and imposed short-selling curbs (5:48 AM ET), and that selling by trend-following systematic funds amplified Thursday's record plunge in Nasdaq 100 market value (5:30 AM ET). The Financial Times reported futures point to small gains at the opening bell (6:10 AM ET). WSJ reported Treasury yields turned higher ahead of the jobs data (6:23 AM ET) and oil fell below $100 a barrel as investors focused on Washington's next move on Iran (3:58 AM ET).

cryptoDriver.text: CoinDesk reported that ETFs shed $430 million after the tech rout.

items.headline: Alibaba sets Nov 18 board meeting for September-quarter results; announcement Nov 19
items.summary: In a Form 6-K filed with the SEC (accepted 6:01 AM ET), Alibaba said its board will meet to discuss unaudited results for the three months and six months ended September 30, 2026, with the results announcement on November 18, 2026 and the results approved and announced on November 19, 2026, per the filing's wording.
